passage:
When the hostel's shared fund came up short, the blame slid toward Aditi. Rohan started it. “She handles the money, doesn't she?” A few people nodded.

Omkar had been about to say nothing. Then Rohan turned to him. “Omkar, you were there, weren't you?” Omkar heard himself say, “Yeah, typical Aditi,” and laughed a little. Everyone else laughed with him.

The relief was instant. He was on the safe side of the room. Aditi picked up her bag and left without a word. Karan, in the corner, kept his eyes on his laptop.

By midnight the warm feeling was gone. Omkar typed a message to Aditi: “I shouldn't have laughed. I know it wasn't fair.” He watched the word “Delivered” sit there.

qa.q: Who did the group blame when the shared fund came up short?
qa.a: The group blamed Aditi, who handles the money.

qa.q: Why did Omkar say “Yeah, typical Aditi” and laugh?
qa.a: Omkar was afraid of becoming the next target, so joining in felt safer than staying quiet.

qa.q: What choice did Omkar make at midnight, and why might it matter?
qa.a: Omkar wrote to Aditi admitting the laugh was unfair, which owns up to the mistake and shows Aditi not everyone agreed.

qa.q: What was it like for Aditi, picking up the bag and leaving without a word?
qa.a: Aditi likely felt hurt and alone, judged by people who were friendly before, and leaving quietly may have been the only way to keep dignity.

grounding: A student joins in blaming a peer to avoid becoming the next target, feels relief at first and then the inner cost.

passage:
“Who left the lab door unlocked?” Tarun asked, arms crossed.

“Yamini, obviously,” said Priya. “She closed up last.”

“I did lock it,” Yamini said. “I checked twice.”

“Sure,” Tarun said. “Jasleen, you were there. Back me up.”

Jasleen looked at the floor. “I mean... she is forgetful sometimes.”

“See?” Tarun said. “Even Jasleen says so.”

“I didn't say it was her,” Jasleen said, quieter. Nobody heard.

Yamini looked at her a long moment. “Right. Fine.” She picked up her bag and left.

Priya laughed. Tarun nodded, satisfied. Jasleen stayed in her chair, her jaw tight, feeling safe and hating it.

qa.q: Who did Priya say had closed up the lab last?
qa.a: Priya said Yamini had closed up last.

qa.q: Why did Jasleen say “she is forgetful sometimes” about Yamini?
qa.a: Jasleen was afraid of being the next target and gave in to Tarun's pressure, even though Jasleen had no proof.

qa.q: What could Jasleen do next after staying in the chair, feeling safe and hating it?
qa.a: Jasleen could find Yamini and admit the remark was unfair, and tell the group there is no evidence about the door.

qa.q: What was Yamini thinking when looking at Jasleen for a long moment?
qa.a: Yamini probably felt betrayed and let down, hoping Jasleen would speak up, and then gave up when nobody did.

grounding: A student under pressure joins in blaming a peer to stay safe, and the relief hides the inner cost.

passage:
I'm Gargi, and there's a joke I made in second year that I still regret.
Our project group missed the submission deadline by a day. At the canteen, everyone started on Irfan. “Irfan was supposed to upload it.” “Irfan's always late.” Actually, the file wasn't ready because none of us had finished our parts.
I could feel where it was going. If I defended him, they'd look at me next. So I laughed and said, “Irfan runs on Irfan Standard Time.” Everyone laughed. The pressure left my chest like air from a balloon.
Irfan smiled weakly and paid for his own tea.
I felt safe for about an hour. Then I felt sick for about a week.

qa.q: What did Gargi joke about Irfan?
qa.a: Gargi said, "Irfan runs on Irfan Standard Time."

qa.q: How did Gargi feel after making the joke?
qa.a: Gargi felt relieved and safe for about an hour, then sick with guilt for about a week.

qa.q: What could Gargi have said instead?
qa.a: Gargi could have said that none of the parts were ready, which was true and would have shared the blame fairly.

qa.q: How might Irfan have felt smiling weakly?
qa.a: He probably felt hurt and alone, blamed for a group failure and laughed at by friends.

grounding: A student recalls joining lightly in blaming a peer out of fear of being next, and the relief hiding how much it cost inside.

passage:
Lab supervisor's note, Microbiology, Week 6.
When the culture plates were found contaminated today, the students quickly agreed that Naveen had left the incubator open. I heard several say it before anyone checked the log.
Rashmi, who works next to him, added, “He's always rushing,” and laughed. Then she went very quiet.
After the others left, Rashmi came back and said, “Sir, I don't actually know it was Naveen. I just didn't want them to start on me. I was near the incubator too.” She looked shaken.
I thanked her for coming back. The log showed the door alarm had failed, not any one student. I will explain this to the whole group tomorrow and speak to Naveen first.

qa.q: What did the log show?
qa.a: The log showed the door alarm had failed, not any one student.

qa.q: Why did Rashmi go very quiet after laughing?
qa.a: She felt guilty and uneasy, having joined the blame out of fear of being targeted next.

qa.q: What did the supervisor do after Rashmi came back?
qa.a: The supervisor thanked her, checked the log, and planned to speak to Naveen first and then the whole group.

qa.q: How might Naveen have felt when everyone blamed him?
qa.a: He probably felt hurt and unfairly singled out, blamed before anyone checked the facts.

grounding: A supervisor's note shows a student joining in blaming a peer out of fear, then admitting the cost to herself.

passage:
Tuesday, 11:40 pm
The college fined our whole class for the noise at the fest. In the class group, people started blaming Kavitha because she was the one who played the speaker. Someone posted, “Thanks Kavitha for the fine 🙄.” Then it was twenty messages.
I sent a laughing emoji. Just one. I wasn't going to write anything, but I knew if I stayed silent someone would say, “Hemant, you were dancing right next to the speaker.” So I laughed.
I felt so relieved when the chat moved on.
Now I can't sleep. I was dancing next to the speaker. We all were. Kavitha hasn't posted anything since 8 pm.
Tomorrow I'll message her. I'll say sorry.
Hemant

qa.q: What did the college fine the class for?
qa.a: The college fined them for the noise at the fest.

qa.q: How did Hemant feel when the chat moved on, and later?
qa.a: Hemant felt relieved when the chat moved on, but later guilty and unable to sleep.

qa.q: Is Hemant's plan a good one, and what else could help?
qa.a: Yes; apologising to Kavitha is a start, and saying in the group that everyone was dancing would share the blame fairly.

qa.q: How might Kavitha be feeling, not posting since 8 pm?
qa.a: She is probably hurt and alone, blamed by twenty messages for something the whole class did.

grounding: A student writes about joining lightly in blaming a classmate out of fear of being next, and the relief hiding the cost.
